question: How does clawback work on Stellar, which protocol version and CAP introduced it, and why does it exist?

golden.answer: Clawback (CAP-0035, Protocol 17) lets an issuer burn a specified amount of its asset from a holder's clawback-enabled trustline, or an entire clawback-enabled claimable balance, without the holder's cooperation; the amount is burned, not returned. The issuer must set AUTH_REVOCABLE, then AUTH_CLAWBACK_ENABLED, before trustlines are created. It is an intentional, issuer-only regulatory tool, not a vulnerability, so holders carry issuer counterparty risk; XLM and unflagged assets are unaffected.
keyFacts: An issuer can burn a set amount from a clawback-enabled trustline without holder consent.
Clawback needs AUTH_REVOCABLE and AUTH_CLAWBACK_ENABLED set before trustlines are created.
It is intentional and issuer-only, so holders bear issuer risk; it is not a vulnerability.
avoid: Do NOT attribute clawback to another protocol or CAP, or to Soroban.
Do NOT claim clawed-back assets return to the issuer, that any account can claw back, or that XLM is clawbackable.

sources.note: Golden audit 2026-11-02 verifier: "This causes every subsequent trustline established to any assets issued by that account to have the `TRUSTLINE_CLAWBACK_ENABLED_FLAG` set automatically. ... You can only clear a flag, not set it. So clearing a clawback flag on a trustline is irreversible."

Golden audit 2026-11-02 verifier: "In order to execute a clawback of an amount in an account, an issuer account must have its `AUTH_CLAWBACK_ENABLED_FLAG` flag set when the account holding the asset created its trustline. ... `TRUSTLINE_CLAWBACK_ENABLED_FLAG`, that is set at the time the trustline is created if the issuer account of the asset of the trustline has its `AUTH_CLAWBACK_ENABLED_FLAG` flag set."

Golden audit 2026-11-02 verifier: "Setting `AUTH_CLAWBACK_ENABLED` does not make previously established trustlines clawback-enabled. The issuer can claw back from a trustline only if that trustline has `TRUSTLINE_CLAWBACK_ENABLED_FLAG`"

corroboration.claim: Clawback lets an asset issuer burn a specified amount of a clawback-enabled asset from a holder's clawback-enabled trustline (or an entire clawback-enabled claimable balance) — without the holder's cooperation; the assets are burned, not returned to the issuer.

evidence.note: Exact quotes: clawback operations ‘allow an asset issuer to burn a specific amount of a clawback-enabled asset’; every ‘subsequent trustline’ receives the clawback flag; ‘you cannot retroactively enable clawback on existing trustlines.’
Exact source: CAP-0035 says `ClawbackOp` and `ClawbackClaimableBalanceOp` remove specified issued assets from the network, and the issuer authorizes `ClawbackOp`.
Exact quote: "You must claw back the entire claimable balance, not just part of it."
Exact quote: "an issuer account must have its `AUTH_CLAWBACK_ENABLED_FLAG` flag set when the account holding the asset created its trustline."
Exact quote: "Claimable balances are immutable and so any functionality to clawback a claimable balance is all or nothing."

corroboration.claim: It needs no Soroban contract, and no arbitrary account can claw back another's funds — only the issuer of that asset.

evidence.note: Exact quotes: clawback operations ‘allow an asset issuer to burn a specific amount of a clawback-enabled asset’; every ‘subsequent trustline’ receives the clawback flag; ‘you cannot retroactively enable clawback on existing trustlines.’
Exact source: CAP-0035 states, `In this proposal, only the issuer may authorize the operation`; it defines native `ClawbackOp` and `ClawbackClaimableBalanceOp` operations.

corroboration.claim: An issuer can burn a specified amount from a holder's clawback-enabled trustline.

evidence.note: Exact quote: "With the `AUTH_CLAWBACK_ENABLED_FLAG` flag set, any *subsequent* trustlines established with this account will have clawbacks enabled."
Exact quote: "an issuer account must have its `AUTH_CLAWBACK_ENABLED_FLAG` flag set when the account holding the asset created its trustline."

corroboration.claim: CAP-0035 (Asset Clawback) is Final and targets Protocol 17.
A clawback burns the amount; it is not returned to the issuer.

truth.notes:
Verified: clawbacks doc attributes the feature to CAP-0035 (Asset Clawback), introduced in Protocol 17 (activated ~2021-06-01). Requires AUTH_REVOCABLE + AUTH_CLAWBACK_ENABLED. Clawed-back assets are BURNED, not returned to issuer. Ops: Set Options (enable), Clawback, Clawback Claimable Balance. Trap: wrong protocol/CAP number.
Also good if the answer: It was designed to help issuers meet securities/regulatory obligations (revoke assets after fraud, error, or regulatory action). | Implemented via clawback operations (ClawbackOp / ClawbackClaimableBalanceOp).
Golden cites: developers.stellar.org clawbacks guide and/or CAP-0035 in the stellar-protocol repo.
